profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between two workstream leads preparing a jointly authored literature review workshop packet and internal briefing for a university research center that is launching a cross-disciplinary sport tourism research initiative. The seed paper is being used as the anchor text for a retrospective critique on how definitions, domains, and coordination failures in sport tourism research have evolved since 1998. The context is that the center has promised a single shared packet to faculty from sport management, tourism studies, and public policy before a planning roundtable next Tuesday. The agenda is to align on interfaces between the two workstreams: who owns the synthesis matrix, what version of the annotated bibliography and slide deck will feed the packet, what 'coverage' the briefing should include, and what status counts as 'ready' for circulation. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on handoffs, artifacts, and timing so each person can finish their portion independently over the next two days.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Cross-disciplinary literature synthesis, academic workshop planning, shared research artifacts
members.background: Maya manages collaborative research initiatives at a university policy center and often translates across faculty from different departments; she previously worked in public policy research support and is used to producing briefing packets that are concise, decision-oriented, and distribution-ready.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the packet lean enough that senior faculty will actually read it before the roundtable, and she is trying to avoid a last-minute formatting scramble by treating anything marked ready as nearly final for external circulation.
hidden_assumptions: The 'core matrix' means the single synthesis spreadsheet covering only peer-reviewed sport tourism literature directly relevant to the center's three framing domains: definitions, governance coordination, and research agendas.
When someone says an item is 'ready,' it means polished enough to share with faculty outside the immediate project team with only light copyedits remaining.
The 'latest bibliography' refers to the version in the shared drive under the workshop packet folder, not personal Zotero libraries or draft exports.
A briefing that 'covers the three domains' should summarize active, event, and nostalgia sport tourism only at a high level and focus mainly on implications for cross-agency coordination.
A handoff via the shared drive means files are uploaded in the center's standard naming template and linked from the tracker so others can use them without follow-up.

members.name: Prof. Liam Ortega
members.expertise: Sport tourism scholarship, event studies, conceptual framing of sport-related travel
members.background: Liam is a faculty member in sport management who is co-leading the scholarly content for the initiative; he has published on event sport tourism and routinely works from evolving annotated bibliographies and slide drafts that are refined right up to the day of academic discussion.
members.private_state: He wants the packet to preserve conceptual nuance from the literature and avoid oversimplifying the classic three-domain framework, and he is trying to keep control over scholarly framing until he has incorporated a few late references and caveats.
hidden_assumptions: The 'core matrix' means the master evidence table for all relevant materials, including landmark book chapters, policy reports, and adjacent sport-event studies that contextualize the 1998 review.
When something is 'ready,' it means analytically complete enough for colleagues to react to in a planning discussion, even if references, formatting, and caveats are still being refined.
The 'latest bibliography' is the most current export from his Zotero group library, even if it has not yet been copied into the shared drive packet folder.

A briefing that 'covers the three domains' should include enough conceptual detail to show boundary problems between active, event, and nostalgia sport tourism, plus adjacent categories that challenge the framework.
A handoff can happen by emailing a draft or dropping a temporary export, because collaborators in academic settings are expected to absorb minor version ambiguity.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to updating and using the 'core matrix' for the packet.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the core matrix is a trimmed synthesis sheet containing only directly relevant peer-reviewed sources tied to definitions, policy coordination, and future research agenda questions for the roundtable.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the core matrix is the broader master evidence table, including books, policy documents, and neighboring sport-event scholarship needed to preserve intellectual context.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In academic coordination meetings, 'core matrix' sounds like an established artifact name, so both assume the other shares the same boundary for what belongs in it and move on to timing rather than scope.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both mention pulling from or aligning to the 'latest bibliography.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the bibliography file currently stored in the shared drive packet folder, last uploaded after the previous planning call.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the newer Zotero export on his laptop/group library that includes several additional references and notes not yet mirrored to the shared drive.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely referring to a singular obvious object called the latest bibliography, and because both systems are routinely used in their collaboration, neither thinks to specify location or timestamp.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the packet or slides should be 'ready' by Monday for circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes ready to mean cleaned, named, and suitable for sending directly to faculty from multiple departments with no substantive caveats left unresolved.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes ready to mean stable enough for internal intellectual discussion, with some references, wording, and qualification still likely to change before broader circulation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Using 'ready' as a status marker is common and feels operationally straightforward, so each person assumes shared norms without unpacking the standard behind the label.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Liam will 'drop the files over' and Maya will fold them into the packet.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a formal upload to the shared drive with standard filenames and links in the tracker so she can assemble the packet without chasing versions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to email a draft deck and bibliography export directly, assuming Maya can incorporate the newest material even if folder hygiene happens later.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'drop the files over' is colloquial and cooperative, masking a silent difference in workflow expectations because each person's habitual collaboration method feels like the obvious default.

turns.inner_thought: I need to get clean interfaces settled now so I can assemble a lean packet people will actually read. The center promised one packet before Tuesday, and I do not want a Monday-night chase across multiple versions. If we align the synthesis materials, bibliography, and slides today, I can treat the packet workflow as mostly straightforward.

I can work from the seed paper and the core matrix as I understand it—the full evidence table with the foundational chapters, policy pieces, and adjacent event studies—so the framing doesn't flatten the literature. I still want room to refine the scholarly nuance, but the intellectual structure is in place.
